lessons.title: Story Time: Looking After a Pet
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss a character's responsibility in a pet-themed story.
success_criteria: I can say what the character did for their pet.
I can say why it was important.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss pets children have or would like.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a story about a child caring for a pet, modelling discussion of responsibility.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record what the character did to look after their pet.
key_questions: What did the character do for their pet?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of responsibility theme — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap ways the character cared for their pet.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how you or a family member cares for a pet.

lessons.title: Addition: Pet Food Bowls
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to add two numbers within 20 using a pet food context.
success_criteria: I can add two numbers.
I can write the number sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model adding using a pet food bowl context (e.g. 6 biscuits plus 5 more).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve addition problems within 20 using a pet context, recording number sentences.
key_questions: Can you write the number sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record addition fluency — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Practise adding using pet toys or snacks as counters.

lessons.title: What Do Pets Need to Survive?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what pets need to stay alive and healthy.
success_criteria: I can name 3 things a pet needs.
I can say why each is important.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children's pets need each day.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss basic needs of pets (food, water, shelter, exercise, love/attention).
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and label what a chosen pet needs to survive and be healthy.

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain why each need matters in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of animal needs — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Help care for a pet at home, or talk about what a pet would need.

lessons.title: Writing a Pet Care Guide
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple instructions for caring for a pet.
success_criteria: I can write what a pet needs.
I can use sequencing words.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing simple instructions for caring for a pet.
lessons.independent_task: Children write a short pet care guide (2-3 steps) for a chosen pet.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instructional writing skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share pet care guides with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Write a care guide for your own pet or a pretend one.

lessons.title: Subtraction: Pet Food Bowls
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to subtract within 20 using a pet food context.
success_criteria: I can subtract two numbers.
I can write the number sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model subtracting using a pet food context (e.g. 10 biscuits, ate 4, how many left?).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve subtraction problems within 20 using a pet context, recording number sentences.
key_questions: Can you write the number sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record subtraction fluency — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Practise subtraction using pet toys or snacks as counters.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Pets
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the needs of two different pets.
success_criteria: I can name a need both pets share.
I can name a need that is different.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing the needs of two pets (e.g. a dog and a fish) using a Venn diagram.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the needs of two pets using a Venn diagram.
key_questions: What need do both pets share?
What is different about their needs?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparison and classification skill — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Compare the needs of two pets or animals you know.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Pet Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read pet-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read pet words.
I can read a sentence about pets.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending pet-themed words (e.g. 'dog', 'cat', 'feed').
lessons.independent_task: Children read pet-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading pet words over the week.

lessons.title: Measuring Pet Food: Capacity
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure and compare capacity using pet food scoops.
success_criteria: I can say which container holds more food.
I can use the words full, empty, half full.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model filling containers with rice/sand (representing pet food) and comparing capacity.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the capacity of different pet food containers, recording which holds more.
key_questions: Is this container full or half full?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record capacity comparison skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare the capacity of two containers at home.

lessons.title: Pet or Wild Animal?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to distinguish between pet and wild animals.
success_criteria: I can say if an animal is usually a pet or wild.
I can explain why.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss the difference between a pet dog and a wild wolf.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the concept of domestication — pets are cared for by humans, wild animals look after themselves.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort animal picture cards into pet/wild, explaining reasoning.
key_questions: Is this animal usually a pet or wild?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for animals that can be both (e.g. rabbits)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of domestication concept — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap pet vs wild animal examples.
lessons.home_link: Talk about whether animals you see are usually pets or wild.

lessons.title: Pet Show and Tell
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to talk about a pet (real or imagined) clearly to the class.
success_criteria: I can describe my pet.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap presenting skills from earlier topics.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes an interesting pet talk (name, appearance, what it needs).
lessons.independent_task: Children present about a real or imagined pet to a small group, answering a question.
key_questions: What does it need to be happy?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language progress — evidence for ENG.SL1.
lessons.plenary: Vote on the most interesting pet fact shared.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about a pet you have or would like.

lessons.title: Sharing Pet Treats Equally
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve sharing problems using a pet treat context.
success_criteria: I can share treats equally between pets.
I can say how many each pet gets.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap sharing fairly from earlier weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model sharing a set of 'treats' equally between toy pets.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve sharing problems using counters and toy pets/pictures.
key_questions: How many treats each if shared fairly?

differentiation.greater_depth: Solve sharing problems within 20 with remainders discussed simply

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early division understanding — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Practise sharing treats or snacks fairly at home.

lessons.title: Being a Responsible Pet Owner
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe what it means to be a responsible pet owner.
success_criteria: I can name a responsibility of pet owners.
I can explain why it matters.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about pet needs.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss responsibilities of pet ownership (feeding, exercise, vet visits, cleaning).
lessons.independent_task: Children create a 'Responsible Pet Owner' poster listing key responsibilities.
key_questions: What is a pet owner's responsibility?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's animal care learning — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Help with a pet responsibility at home if you have a pet.

lessons.title: Pets Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about pets and their needs.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about pets, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why is it important to look after pets well?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on pet facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Addition, Subtraction, Sharing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply addition, subtraction and sharing skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can add and subtract within 20.
I can share fairly.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of addition, subtraction, and sharing.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: addition, subtraction, sharing problems.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 22 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N2/N3.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising addition and subtraction over the weekend.

lessons.title: Pets Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about pets and their needs.
success_criteria: I can name what a pet needs.
I can describe a responsible pet owner behaviour.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering pet needs, comparisons, and responsibilities.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Caring for Pets' display.

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note animal care understanding progress — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about pets with your family.
